transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix socket or WebSocket (?token=...). Standard ACP methods pass through to the session's agent; _acpmux/* methods are the multiplexer's own.

acpNotes.initialize: The result's _meta.acpmux carries operations: string[] (the handoff and permission-group methods this daemon serves; clients gate each UI on its methods) and handoff: {maxCapsuleBytes: 65536}. features includes permissionGroups when permission groups are available.
acpNotes.session/new: params._meta.acpmux.adopt {harness?: string, agentSessionId: string, ifLive?: "refuse" | "fork" | "open"} adopts a Claude Code or Codex session started outside acpmux: the id must be a bare id found in the harness's own store (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude projects, CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex sessions), else invalid params. cwd defaults to the session's recorded cwd (Claude refuses a different one). The first turn resumes it (claude --resume, or session/load). Adopting an id twice returns the existing acpmux session. A session live in another process (a process outside acpmux whose command line names the id, or a transcript written in the last 2 minutes) is refused with error data {reason: "adopt.live", details: {signal: "process" | "recentWrite", pid?, command?, agoSeconds?, canFork}} unless ifLive is "open" (adopt anyway) or "fork" (Claude only: a new conversation from claude --resume <id> --fork-session). Recorded as mux adopted {agentSessionId, fork?: true}. A harness name that is a folder profile (.cmux/harnesses/<id>.toml in cwd or a parent; BRING-YOUR-OWN-HARNESS H4) that may not start yet is refused with invalid params; data {reason: harness.needs_trust (answer the folder's Trust question) | harness.needs_enable (show the Enable harness sheet: _acpmux/harness_enable), harness: string (the id), folder: string (the canonical folder that holds .cmux/harnesses)}. A Web or peer connection and an invalid file get no data.
acpNotes.session/prompt: params._meta.acpmux {promptId?: string, steer?: boolean}. On Claude Code harnesses a text block's cache_control reaches the API unchanged; other extra block fields are dropped. The response stays at the end of the turn and gains _meta.acpmux {promptId, turnId, turnSeq} next to the agent's own _meta. The prompting connection gets _acpmux/prompt_accepted as soon as the prompt is recorded.
acpNotes.session/cancel: A notification, as ACP defines it. Sent as a request (with an id) it is answered with {} once the cancel reaches the agent, also when no turn runs.
acpNotes.session/update: Live agent updates arrive with sessionId set to the acpmux id and _meta.acpmux {seq, at, kind} merged into the agent's own _meta (the agent's keys are kept). session/load replays add replay: true.

_acpmux/web_modes.note: Read only. The native relay reads the guard's own table and lists here instead of copying them.

_acpmux/web_token_rotate.note: Replaces the saved dashboard token (config.json, 0600) and the token the listener checks, at once. Web and Peer connections, which presented the old token, are closed; LocalApp connections stay. CLI: acpmux web --rotate-token.

_acpmux/harnesses.errors: invalid params when cwd is not absolute
_acpmux/harnesses.note: Folder harness profiles (BRING-YOUR-OWN-HARNESS H4) are read on each request with cwd; they are not watched, so _acpmux/harnesses_changed never reports them.

_acpmux/reload_config.result: {reloaded: true, harnesses: string[], defaultHarness: string|null, retainedProfiles: string[], modelProbePending: true}; replaces catalog config without stopping sessions

_acpmux/harness_enable.result: without sha256: {prompt: {id, folder, path, state: needs-enable|enabled, trust, argv: string[], program: string|null (what the command resolves to now), env: [{key, source: plain|keychain|env, value? (plain only), item? (keychain), variable? (env)}], checkedFiles: string[] (files inside the folder whose bytes are part of sha256), warnings: string[], sha256, diagnostics, text (the CLI's confirmation text)}}; with sha256: {enabled: FolderProfile}
_acpmux/harness_enable.errors: the folder has no trusted answer, the file is invalid or would replace a catalog harness, or the file changed after the prompt (sha256 differs: show the prompt again)
_acpmux/harness_enable.note: Folder harness profiles (BRING-YOUR-OWN-HARNESS H4). session/new refusals with data.reason harness.needs_enable {harness, folder} name the id and folder to ask for. The unix socket and the local app only; Web and peer connections are refused, also for the prompt. The local app sends sha256 only after a fresh user gesture on its Enable harness sheet. Showing the prompt writes nothing; a recorded confirmation covers sessions whose folder is inside `folder`, until any byte of the file, its icon or a checked file changes.

_acpmux/defaults.result: {families: {family: {kind, profile, error, profiles, model, effort, policy, prefer, env}}, defaults} or one entry
_acpmux/defaults.note: session/new takes _meta.acpmux.harness (a family or profile: the head of -m HEAD/MODEL), .preset, .model, .effort, .policy, .name. Explicit values win over the preset, which wins over profile then family defaults.

params.name: string?
params.set: {harness (family or profile), model?, effort?, policy?, env?, args? (string[]: argv words appended to the harness command, no shell; an allowlist: on Claude Code --tools "", --strict-mcp-config, --no-session-persistence, else none), systemPrompt? models.name: string
models.contextWindow: number? (these from a profile file or the catalog)

params.limit: number? default 2000 (counts only records that pass kinds)
params.eventStream: boolean? (live records of this session arrive only as _acpmux/event, filtered by kinds; no session/update)

result.hasMore: boolean (older matching records exist; with afterSeq alone: newer ones)

_acpmux/attach.note: Subscribes this connection to the session's events and counts it as attached (clears unread). Without afterSeq the page is the newest `limit` records. Attaching again replaces this connection's eventStream and kinds for the session.

_acpmux/watch.note: Receive _acpmux/session_changed for every session, _acpmux/harnesses_changed when the harness catalog reloads from a profile change, and _acpmux/permission_pending (via: "watch") for local sessions this connection is not attached to.

params.beforeSeq: number? (page backwards: the newest `limit` matching records before it)
params.limit: number? default 5000 (counts only records that pass kinds)

result.hasMore: boolean (backwards: older matching records exist; forwards: newer ones below beforeSeq)

errors.cursor_future: afterSeq is beyond the last event

params.sessions: string[]? (empty = every running or waiting session on every host)

result.sessions: SessionSummary[] with resolved: boolean and matched: string[]

_acpmux/warm.note: Starts and initializes one live agent child for each of the most recent requested project sessions; it does not create or select sessions.

params.harness: string? (a family or profile; default the default harness)
params.wait: boolean? default false (answer once the hinted session is ready or failed)

result.reason: string? (accepted false: the pool is off)
result.superseded: boolean? (wait: a newer hint replaced this one)

_acpmux/prewarm.errors: invalid_params over a remote-origin connection (never pooled)
_acpmux/prewarm.note: Hints the harness the pane is about to switch to. After the debounce (pool.debounceMs, default 150) only the newest hint counts: a hidden session for it starts in that cwd (agent host, initialize and the harness session done). Per cwd at most two are kept: the harness used before the current one and the hinted one. A session/new of exactly that shape (cwd, harness, preset, argv, system prompt, env and credentials, account) takes it at once. Hidden sessions never appear in _acpmux/sessions or liveAgents and leave nothing in the store unless taken; _acpmux/status pool lists them as {entries: [{harness, preset, cwd, roles, state}], rssBytes}. They exit after pool.idleMinutes (default 10) unused, under pool.maxRssMb (default 1024, oldest first) and at shutdown.

_acpmux/permission_groups.note: Read on reconnect/lag before retrying an identical decision body/key. Unknown groupId is not_found.

_acpmux/permission_group_respond.errors: collecting, stale_revision, already_resolved, policy_changed (-32000, data.group); key_conflict (-32602); not_found (-32002)
_acpmux/permission_group_respond.note: Atomically validates sealed membership and single-use options before responding to any underlying ACP request. allow_chat grants later eligible requests in this chat until agent stop/restart; deny policy/rules override and grants never copy to fork/handoff. Repeat identical key/body replays a retained receipt; another body conflicts. Interactive and unknown requests remain individual.

_acpmux/permission_chat_revoke.note: Revokes future chat approvals; already accepted operations are not undone.

params.rules: {autoApprove?: string[], autoDeny?: string[], ask?: string[], default?: 'approve'|'deny'|'ask'} | null

params.harness: string (the target: a family or profile of another harness)
params.handoffKey: string (repeat safety: the same key returns the same record and never a second target)

_acpmux/handoff_prepare.errors: source_busy (a turn runs, prompts are queued or a permission waits), same_harness, policy_unmappable, checkpoint_unattested, key_conflict (-32602, with handoff: the handoffKey already names a handoff from another source or to another harness)
_acpmux/handoff_prepare.note: Captures the source's transcript up to its current seq, newest messages first within maxCapsuleBytes (the oldest are cut), and creates the target session in the source's cwd with the source's policy (same) or the next stricter one (narrower: approve-all > approve-edits > approve-reads > ask > deny-all). Same or narrower is guaranteed for the acpmux permission policy only, not for harness modes, which are not mapped across harnesses. The target is tagged handoffKey=<key>; a repeat prepare whose record was never saved adopts that live, never-prompted target instead of creating a second one. Sends no prompt to the target and never modifies the source.

_acpmux/handoff_get.note: With sessionId: the handoff the session is the target of, else the newest one not discarded that it is the source of, else null (an ordinary session). After a reconnect, read this before retrying anything.

params.checkpoint: CheckpointInput | null ? (absent keeps it, null clears it)

_acpmux/handoff_draft.errors: stale_revision (with handoff), not_draft (with handoff), discarded (with handoff), checkpoint_unattested, capsule_too_large, not_found
_acpmux/handoff_draft.note: The same draftKey again (one of the last 8 writes) answers with the revision and capsule that write produced, state and updatedAt current, and never writes twice. A stale revision whose content equals the current draft succeeds without a new revision; other content is refused with stale_revision.

params.capsule: {text: string, memoryRefs?: string[]}? (absent keeps the draft)

_acpmux/handoff_start.errors: checkpoint_required, checkpoint_unattested, stale_revision (with handoff), capsule_too_large, already_started (another promptId after the first start; with handoff), discarded (with handoff), not_found
_acpmux/handoff_start.note: Records state starting with the promptId, then sends the capsule text (plus a block naming the checkpoint and memory references) to the target once, as session/prompt with _meta.acpmux {promptId, resend: true}, and answers once the target records the prompt (the turn runs on). After a timeout, read handoff_get; in state starting or started, call start again with the same promptId: the daemon finds the prompt in the record or the target's log (also after a restart) and answers already_started without sending again. A start refused before the target records the prompt returns the record to draft and keeps its promptId, which a later start reuses by default. Test-only fault (uncertain_delivery is produced only by this hook): with ACPMUX_TEST_DROP_HANDOFF_START_REPLY=1 in the daemon's environment a first start sends the prompt, leaves the record starting and answers an error with reason uncertain_delivery instead of the receipt, so a retry exercises reconciliation.

_acpmux/handoff_discard.note: Closes the target, which has never been prompted. The source stays intact. Discarding twice is fine.

_acpmux/event.note: Every mux record of an attached session. With attach eventStream: every record that passes kinds, agent session/update notifications included (the original notification in msg, its sessionId the agent's own).

params.kind: string (the record kind, or queue for queued/dequeued, permission_resolved for permission_auto, purged)

_acpmux/session_changed.note: For watchers: status, queue, permission, turn and policy changes, and peer sessions that appear, change or leave.

_acpmux/harnesses_changed.note: To watchers (_acpmux/watch) when a harness profile file, a managed or user profile folder, or cmux.json changed and the catalog reloaded (debounced 200 ms, no polling). Ask _acpmux/harnesses for the details. Folder profiles (.cmux/harnesses in a workspace) are not watched and never trigger it; ask _acpmux/harnesses {cwd} again.

_acpmux/permission_pending.note: To attached connections, and to watchers that are not attached (via: watch). Remote sessions reach watchers only through session_changed.

catalog.changed.note: Sent to every connection (no watch or attach needed) when the model catalog in use changes. Read _acpmux/models or _acpmux/harnesses again.

params.promptId: string (the client's _meta.acpmux.promptId, or one acpmux generated)

_acpmux/prompt_accepted.note: Sent only to the connection that sent session/prompt, as soon as the daemon records the prompt (the queued or user_message record). Not relayed for sessions on a peer.

HarnessProfile.fallback: string? (profile to move to on limit or auth errors)

SessionSummary.name: string
SessionSummary.stateSeq: number (bumps on status, permission and turn changes)
SessionSummary.unread: boolean (a turn ended while no client was attached)
SessionSummary.lastTurn: {turnId, promptId, status, stopReason?, errorText?, errorSource?, endedAt} | null
SessionSummary.queue: [{promptId, turnId, client, prompt, queuedAt}] prompts waiting for the running turn
SessionSummary.turn: {startedAt, client, prompt, turnId, promptId, turnSeq} | null (the running turn)

types.SessionDetail: SessionSummary plus modes, configOptions, models, agentInfo, agentCapabilities, usage, pending: [{permissionId, request, groupId, turnId}] (groupId and turnId are string|null), rulesJson

Event.kind: string (method, sessionUpdate value, or mux kind)

turn_result.errorText: string? (why the turn failed; a terminal error the harness reported in-band, such as Codex _meta.codex.error without willRetry, fails the turn and the prompt is answered with that error)
turn_result.errorChunkSeqs: number[]? (the trailing agent_message_chunk records whose text is exactly errorText: hide them, show the error)
turn_result.detail: string? (outcome_unknown when the daemon restarted mid-turn)

types.EventKinds: string[]: each entry is a category or an exact record kind; a record passes when any entry matches. Categories: transcript (agent session/update except .replay, usage_update, available_commands_update, current_mode_update, config_option_update; plus mux user_message, queued, dequeued, turn_started, turn_result, permission_request, permission_auto, permission_decision, permission_group, permission_chat_allowance, message_superseded, failover, forked, imported, mode, model, stopped, exited), mux (every mux record), wire (in/out requests, responses, harness lines and .replay records), all.

turn_started.note: turnSeq of the turn is this record's seq

turn_end.note: legacy pair of turn_result; turn_error likewise carries {error, code, turnId, turnSeq}

message_superseded.note: Recorded before the first chunk of the redelivered message. Drop the chunks of oldMessageId. Only Codex signals this (session_info_update _meta.codex.error.willRetry while a message streams); other harnesses give no signal.

Enforcement.policy: string (always the acpmux permission policy id: ask|approve-reads|approve-edits|approve-all|deny-all, the session's own or the daemon default; comparable across harnesses)
Enforcement.label: native_policy
Enforcement.detail: string|null (names the harness's current mode, e.g. "codex mode read-only; acpmux policy approve-reads; host isolation unverified")
Enforcement.note: On every SessionSummary. What limits the session's agent as far as acpmux can tell; v1 never claims host isolation or infers a sandbox from a mode name, and harness modes are reported, not mapped.

CheckpointInput.note: The daemon stamps attestedBy and attestedAt; a ref without attest: true, or an empty ref, is checkpoint_unattested.

Coverage.note: How much of each item reaches the target, per session; only inside a handoff (an ordinary session has no coverage).

Handoff.revision: number (1 at prepare, +1 per accepted draft write)
Handoff.source: {sessionId, harness, cwd, coverage: Coverage[], enforcement: Enforcement, seq: number (the source's seq at prepare)}
Handoff.target: {sessionId, harness, cwd (the source's), coverage: Coverage[], enforcement: Enforcement}
Handoff.capsule: {text: string (the target's first message, at most maxBytes UTF-8 bytes), context: {fromSeq, toSeq, truncated, bytes (transcript bytes in text), totalBytes (transcript bytes up to toSeq)}, checkpoint: Checkpoint|null, memoryRefs: string[], maxBytes: 65536}
Handoff.turnId: string|null (set once the target records the turn)
Handoff.note: Persisted as handoffs/<handoffId>.json in the daemon home (in memory with --memory) and loaded on start.

HandoffError.data: {reason: source_busy|same_harness|policy_unmappable|checkpoint_required|checkpoint_unattested|capsule_too_large|stale_revision|not_draft|already_started|discarded|not_found|key_conflict|uncertain_delivery (test hook only), handoff?: Handoff}; capsule_too_large adds {limit, bytes}

daemon.readiness: acpmux daemon run binds the socket and --listen address before importing the login shell environment or checking launchers. --ready-fd N writes one line {ready: true, pid, socket, listen, webUrl} to descriptor N and closes it; the log also gets "acpmux ready {...}". _acpmux/status answers at once and reports ready and loginEnv.
daemon.shutdown: The daemon clears any signal mask it inherits, so a launcher that blocks SIGTERM cannot keep it alive. SIGTERM, SIGINT and _acpmux/shutdown remove the socket, detach every agent that runs under an agent host (it keeps running, with its turn and permission prompts, for the next daemon to adopt), stop every other agent (SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL to the group after 2 s), save sessions, sync the store and exit, within 5 s. _acpmux/shutdown {endAgents: true} ends hosted agents too, except those of keepSessions, and records each turn in progress as turn_result {status: cancelled, detail: quit}.

exitCodes.5: every permission in the turn was denied
